newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IBCA accords AA- rating to S.Africa INCA bonds.
newsitem.headline: IBCA accords AA- rating to S.Africa INCA bonds.

text.p: International rating agency IBCA on Monday accorded a domestic long-term AA- rating to bonds issued by South African capital provider Infrastructure Finance Corporation Limited (INCA).
IBCA said in a statement the rating indicated a low expectation of investment risk.
INCA, which was launched on Monday, would provide capital to a broad range of participants in local and provincial government, water and other utilities as well as dedicated infrastructure providers.
It would issue five, 10 and 15 year bonds in order to raise the necessary finances for on-lending, IBCA said.

"INCA's asset base shall be subjected to a rigorous credit model in the absence of a formal IBCA rating. This model applies both qualitative and quantitative aspects and will be utilised to determine the level of capital which INCA will be required to hold against loans to counter parties," IBCA said.
In view of the developing situation in local government in South Africa, a conservative risk weighting had been applied to loans made by INCA in the determination of capital adequacy requirements.

Earlier on Monday INCA said it intends raising 12 billion rand over the next seven years through the issue of various capital market bonds, the first tranche of which will be listed on the Bond Exchange of South Africa before the end of the year.

Partners in INCA are First National Bank Holdings Ltd and Southern Life Association Ltd each with a 20 percent stake, black-owned Msele Financial Holdings Ltd with 10 percent, the Women's Investment Portfolio with five, Old Mutual with 10, and the UK's Commonwealth Development Corp with 20 percent.
